3332de88-caf3-4a31-b702-11eb7490c215.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another
COURT: Supreme Court of India
CITATION: (2014) 8 SCC 273 : AIR 2014 SC 2756 : 2014 Cri LJ 3707
BENCH: Chandramauli Kr. Prasad and Pinaki Chandra Ghose, JJ.
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 2014-07-02
DOCUMENT TYPE: judgment

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

c8e2cc4d-decb-4fe3-9155-5d127e5faf24.document:
[Para 3]
The petitioner in this special leave petition seeks anticipatory bail in a case registered under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. The petitioner apprehends arrest following marital discord with his wife, who alleged demands for dowry.

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

1372bd58-c10b-4a01-a18f-04b6cca1be6d.document:
[Para 5]
Arrest brings humiliation, curtails freedom, and casts scars forever. Lawmakers know that arrest is a tool of harassment and oppression in hands of unscrupulous police officers. No arrest can be made because it is lawful for the police officer to do so. The existence of the power to arrest is one thing, the justification for the exercise of it is quite another. A police officer must not make arrests in a routine manner upon mere allegation of commission of an offence.

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

8c293e7d-0d71-48b0-b705-72b120d2b326.document: [Para 7] Section 41 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 provides the conditions under which police may arrest without warrant. In respect of offences punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years, arrest must not be made routinely. The police officer must be satisfied that such arrest is necessary: (a) to prevent such person from committing any further offence; or (b) for proper investigation of the offence; or (c) to prevent such person from causing the evidence of the offence to disappear or tampering with such evidence; or

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

cc0a69ef-6f23-4c9a-b967-0224ed23d10e.document: person from causing the evidence of the offence to disappear or tampering with such evidence; or (d) to prevent such person from making any inducement, threat, or promise to witnesses; or (e) to ensure his presence before the court whenever required.

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

18745961-42eb-474e-8630-c37479698b66.document:
[Para 8]
Section 41A of the Code provides that where the arrest of a person is not required under Section 41(1), the police officer shall issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made to appear before him. Where such a notice is issued, it shall be the duty of that person to comply with the terms of the notice. So long as he complies with the notice, he shall not be arrested unless the police officer records reasons in writing.

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

26dc204d-dc14-4a23-9229-1bc5cbc3861d.document: [Para 11] To ensure that police officers do not arrest accused persons unnecessarily and Magistrates do not authorise detention casually, this court issues the following mandatory directions: 1. All State Governments shall instruct police officers not to automatically arrest when a case under Section 498A IPC or offences with punishment up to 7 years is registered. 2. Police officers shall be provided with a checklist containing specified sub-clauses under Section 41(1)(b)(ii). 3. The police officer shall forward the checklist duly filled and furnish reasons necessitating arrest when producing

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

d5581cc6-3273-4b59-88aa-75324ebb97b0.document: shall forward the checklist duly filled and furnish reasons necessitating arrest when producing the accused before the Magistrate. 4. The Magistrate shall peruse the report and record independent satisfaction before authorising further detention. 5. Notice of appearance in terms of Section 41A CrPC shall be served on the accused within two weeks from the date of institution of the case. 6. Failure to comply with these directions shall render the police officer and Magistrate liable for departmental action and contempt of court.

metadata.document_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

db0a7363-aea9-4a92-ae18-c907c1ec17a3.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
COURT: Parliament of India / Statutory Enactment
CITATION: Act No. 46 of 2023, Section 482
BENCH: Statutory Provision
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 2023-12-25
DOCUMENT TYPE: statute

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

4c30c196-87ff-4977-9d8f-f35a45454f06.document: [Section 482(1)] Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest: Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction under this section that in the event of such arrest he shall be released on bail; and that Court may, after taking into consideration, inter alia, the following factors, namely: (i) the nature and gravity of the accusation; (ii) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

42213d5d-ad94-4d5d-b5cf-9d44908640a2.document: of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv) where the accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested, either reject the application forthwith or issue an interim order for the grant of bail.

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

4e666873-7a43-4bbc-8112-e5f544de3c19.document: [Section 482(2)] When the High Court or Court of Session makes a direction under sub-section (1), it may include such conditions in such directions in the light of the facts of the particular case, as it may think fit, including: (i) a condition that the person shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required; (ii) a condition that the person shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer; (iii)

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

46bfd0c2-3592-4024-b161-2d052a54fb03.document: case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer; (iii) a condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court; (iv) such other condition as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of section 480, as if the bail were granted under that section.

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

c6f6cae9-53dc-4cb0-aac4-677a3ad99df9.document:
[Section 482(3)]
The presence of the applicant seeking anticipatory bail shall not be mandatory at the time of hearing of the application, unless the Court considers it necessary in the interest of justice.

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

3d86f7f3-cafb-4a2d-826c-e7e1c0c86168.document:
[Section 482(4)]
Nothing in this section shall apply to any case involving the arrest of any person on accusation of having committed an offence under section 65 or section 66 or sub-section (2) of section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

metadata.document_title: Section 482, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

960cca9c-db35-48ab-8cb0-8cddcb445819.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Article 21, Constitution of India
COURT: Constituent Assembly of India / Constitutional Law
CITATION: Constitution of India, Part III, Article 21
BENCH: Constitutional Guarantee
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 1950-01-26
DOCUMENT TYPE: statute

metadata.document_title: Article 21, Constitution of India

da1debb7-78b0-44de-b6e3-130e3d6fd9a4.document:
[Article 21]
Protection of life and personal liberty:
No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

metadata.document_title: Article 21, Constitution of India

7afbe738-9c1a-4bc9-a191-9b74248c9f36.document:
[Constitutional Jurisprudence]
In Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248, the Supreme Court ruled that the 'procedure established by law' under Article 21 must be right, just, and fair, and not arbitrary, fanciful, or oppressive. A procedure that deprives an individual of their personal liberty through unjust or mechanical arrest violates the core guarantee of Article 21.

metadata.document_title: Article 21, Constitution of India

c2f2de63-f3ce-41ae-807e-1c5260cdcc99.document: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is intrinsically linked to Article 21. As observed in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and affirmed in Sushila Aggarwal, the judicial discretion to grant pre-arrest bail protects innocent citizens from the irreparable trauma, stigmatization, and indignity of unwarranted incarceration pending trial.

metadata.document_title: Article 21, Constitution of India

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

6b0c1507-eef5-493a-8498-5a00a06f93e7.document: [Section 438(1)] Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest: Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction under this section that in the event of such arrest he shall be released on bail; and that Court may, after taking into consideration, inter alia, the following factors, namely: (i) the nature and gravity of the accusation; (ii) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

7ea86739-9dd0-4709-90a1-6488c899fe56.document: of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv) where the accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested, either reject the application forthwith or issue an interim order for the grant of anticipatory bail.

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

b27901f6-e440-473f-8e3a-3661b4266e35.document: [Section 438(2)] When the High Court or the Court of Session makes a direction under sub-section (1), it may include such conditions in such directions in the light of the facts of the particular case, as it may think fit, including: (i) a condition that the person shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required; (ii) a condition that the person shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

860af9d1-255a-4486-a939-d408bf6fbe95.document: of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer; (iii) a condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court; (iv) such other condition as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of section 437, as if the bail were granted under that section.

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

1aa88f5d-84be-4e57-8863-53437f2f0992.document:
[Section 438(3)]
If such person is thereafter arrested without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station on such accusation, and is prepared either at the time of arrest or at any time while in the custody of such officer to give bail, he shall be released on bail; and if a Magistrate taking cognizance of such offence decides that a warrant should issue in the first instance against that person, he shall issue a bailable warrant in conformity with the direction of the Court under sub-section (1).

metadata.document_title: Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

38d21f8b-0d8c-49f7-b368-e1e5f3297f61.document:
[Section 438(4)]
Nothing in this section shall apply to any case involving the arrest of any person on accusation of having committed an offence under sub-section (3) of section 376 or section 376AB or section 376DA or section 376DB of the Indian Penal Code.

8f07c620-7d82-479f-b66b-e55d3670f568.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab
COURT: Supreme Court of India (Constitution Bench)
CITATION: (1980) 2 SCC 565 : AIR 1980 SC 1632 : 1980 Cri LJ 1125
BENCH: Y.V. Chandrachud, C.J., P.N. Bhagwati, N.L. Untwalia, V.D. Tulzapurkar, and A.P. Sen, JJ.
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 1980-04-09
DOCUMENT TYPE: judgment

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

ee1a0b96-84b6-4621-9505-484ec2155095.document:
[Para 1]
This appeal by special leave involves the interpretation of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which confers power on the High Court and the Court of Session to grant anticipatory bail. The question before this Constitution Bench is regarding the scope, nature, and limitations governing the exercise of judicial discretion under Section 438 of the Code.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

e59773c5-3cf1-498b-a010-be7acb9239d8.document:
[Para 7]
Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 makes a departure from the previous Code of 1898 by introducing a provision for the grant of anticipatory bail. The Law Commission of India in its 41st Report recommended the introduction of this provision in order to safeguard the personal liberty of citizens against malicious, frivolous, or politically motivated accusations intended to humiliate, disgrace, or incarcerate individuals before trial.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

d33683e2-f838-4a4d-b680-6d03fb1a641a.document:
[Para 12]
The power under Section 438 is of an extraordinary character and must be exercised with due care and circumspection. However, the discretion vested in the High Court and the Court of Session is not bound by rigid or inflexible fetters. The Legislature intentionally refrained from circumscribing the discretion with rigid rules. The High Court and the Court of Session must be left free to exercise their judicial discretion according to the facts and circumstances of each individual case.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

0e91ad4e-7d38-4448-84e6-47b7611e38d0.document: [Para 15] While considering an application for anticipatory bail under Section 438, the court must carefully evaluate several critical factors: First, the nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role attributed to the applicant. Second, the antecedents of the applicant, including whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction in respect of any cognizable offence. Third, the possibility of the applicant fleeing from justice or absconding. Fourth, whether the accusation has been made with the ulterior motive of injuring, humiliating, or tarnishing the reputation of the

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

54da4bb7-fcc0-48f0-932d-426ac1958c10.document: been made with the ulterior motive of injuring, humiliating, or tarnishing the reputation of the applicant by having him so arrested. Fifth, the likelihood of the accused tampering with evidence, threatening witnesses, or otherwise obstructing the course of fair investigation and trial.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

b472f16e-4253-4788-b57d-daa468bdede0.document:
[Para 19]
A blanket order of anticipatory bail cannot and ought not to be granted. A blanket order that an applicant shall be released on bail whenever he may be arrested in future for any offence whatsoever serves as a charter of lawlessness and impedes the legitimate functions of the investigating agency. An applicant seeking anticipatory bail must demonstrate a reasonable belief and apprehension of arrest founded on specific and tangible facts relating to a concrete offence.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

60d11e85-740c-48dd-bea8-aba713ca07c6.document: [Para 26] The court granting anticipatory bail is empowered under Section 438(2) to impose suitable conditions. Such conditions include: (i) A condition that the person shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required; (ii) A condition that the person shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer; (iii) A condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

521af92a-02d5-44f0-b722-49566a8863ff.document: (iii) A condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the court; and (iv) Such other condition as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of Section 437, as if the bail were granted under that section.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

9cbe238f-b281-4a02-b096-72da266ef594.document:
[Para 31]
Anticipatory bail does not place the accused beyond the reach of the investigating machinery. If custodial interrogation becomes indispensable on discovery of new material during the course of investigation, the prosecution is always at liberty to apply to the court for cancellation or modification of the anticipatory bail order under Section 439(2) of the Code.

metadata.document_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

610e1a27-425b-4d44-986b-ac337a6add59.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another
COURT: Supreme Court of India
CITATION: (2022) 10 SCC 51 : 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825 : AIR 2022 SC 3386
BENCH: Sanjay Kishan Kaul and M.M. Sundresh, JJ.
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 2022-07-11
DOCUMENT TYPE: judgment

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

968d5189-65d3-456b-9428-57c33144783a.document:
[Para 2]
The present proceedings arise out of persistent concerns regarding overcrowding of prisons in India, where over two-thirds of the inmate population comprises undertrial prisoners. This judgment issues comprehensive guidelines to streamline the procedure for grant of bail, emphasizing that the rule is bail and not jail.

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

5674ed66-4429-4bce-9d2a-5bf79d07fdb7.document: [Para 18] Offences are broadly categorized into four groups for the purpose of bail consideration: Category A: Offences punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or less not falling under Category B and D. For these offences, ordinary summons or appearance notice under Section 41A CrPC should be issued, and routine arrests avoided. Category B: Offences punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for more than 7 years. Bail applications to be decided on merits on appearance. Category C: Offences punishable under special Acts containing stringent negative bail conditions (such as

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

ec975b0c-1fff-4e68-888f-19b7af06654d.document: C: Offences punishable under special Acts containing stringent negative bail conditions (such as NDPS Act S. 37, PMLA S. 45, UAPA S. 43D(5), Companies Act S. 212(6)). Category D: Economic offences not covered by special Acts. The gravity of financial loss to the public exchequer and systemic ramification must be considered.

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

dc571059-1df6-4eee-8e97-dd31a76685c9.document:
[Para 26]
While dealing with applications under Section 438 of the CrPC, courts must balance the need for custodial interrogation against the fundamental right to personal liberty under Article 21. Economic offences do not fall under a single blanket rule; where the accused has cooperated with the investigation, furnished requisite documentary records, and has deep roots in society without flight risk, anticipatory bail should not be refused merely on the ground of an economic accusation.

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

32d4e5d7-def9-4cc5-a174-1ba34d82167c.document:
[Para 33]
Courts must not impose mechanical or excessively harsh conditions while granting bail. Requiring local sureties or exorbitant monetary bonds that an impoverished undertrial cannot furnish defeats the very purpose of bail and violates Article 21 of the Constitution.

metadata.document_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another

fc111df2-ebb7-4e78-a480-bcea31fc6b12.document:
DOCUMENT TITLE: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another
COURT: Supreme Court of India (Constitution Bench)
CITATION: (2020) 5 SCC 1 : 2020 SCC OnLine SC 98 : AIR 2020 SC 831
BENCH: Arun Mishra, Indira Banerjee, Vineet Saran, M.R. Shah, and S. Ravindra Bhat, JJ.
DATE OF JUDGMENT: 2020-01-29
DOCUMENT TYPE: judgment

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

b119ff6b-e595-42c4-b11f-326bcc698bde.document:
[Para 5]
The primary questions referred to this Constitution Bench are:
(1) Whether the protection granted to a person under Section 438 CrPC should be limited to a fixed period so as to enable the person to surrender before the trial court and seek regular bail; and
(2) Whether the life of an anticipatory bail order should end automatically upon the filing of the charge sheet under Section 173(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure or upon the summoning of the accused by the trial court.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

5ee008b7-1143-4e4c-a559-e247b977738e.document:
[Para 63]
On question No. 1, this court holds that the protection granted under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 should not ordinarily be limited to a fixed period. The life of an anticipatory bail order does not automatically end when the charge sheet or final report is filed by the police under Section 173 CrPC. The order of anticipatory bail can continue till the conclusion of the trial, unless there are exceptional or special circumstances requiring the court to limit its duration.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

714c46cc-7596-4138-b97a-55e3fc284353.document:
[Para 74]
Judicial discretion should be exercised flexibly. When the High Court or Sessions Court considers an application for anticipatory bail, it is open to the court to impose conditions or restrict the duration if the specific facts of the case demand such limitation. However, limiting the order of anticipatory bail invariably in all cases is contrary to the legislative intent of Section 438 CrPC and the ratio laid down in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

c0608659-fde0-4bd0-b50e-f7267cf9bb48.document:
[Para 78]
On question No. 2, the Constitution Bench clarifies that the mere filing of a charge sheet under Section 173(2) CrPC or the taking of cognizance by the magistrate does not ipso facto terminate or extinguish an order of anticipatory bail. The accused is not obligated to surrender and apply afresh for regular bail merely because the charge sheet has been submitted to the court.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

e28b5b11-8a12-4e0a-a6a6-811a54215b9c.document:
[Para 82]
It is also reiterated that anticipatory bail granted to an accused can always be cancelled or recalled by the High Court or Sessions Court under Section 439(2) CrPC if the accused breaches any bail condition, tampers with witness testimonies, intimidates victims, absconds, or misuses his liberty in any manner that prejudices a fair trial.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

17ec9cce-25d0-4a04-819b-31b128599946.document:
[Para 91]
In conclusion, personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution is a paramount value. Section 438 CrPC embodies this constitutional value by providing a procedural shield against unjustified arrests, while balancing the imperative requirements of state investigation and public interest.

metadata.document_title: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another
